topic: What interference mitigation techniques are viable for overlapping service transmissions across geographically dispersed ground stations?
consensus_response: In geographically dispersed ground stations, precise array factor design minimizes overlap in rural areas with sparse coverage, reducing interference at minimal cost. However, in urban environments, sophisticated beamforming techniques like spatial multiplexing and adaptive modulation & coding (AMC) are essential to combat high traffic density and maintain service quality. Machine Learning (ML)-based Interference Mitigation can further optimize these techniques by dynamically adjusting system parameters based on environmental conditions and network requirements. Advanced Modulation Techniques, such as Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) and Single-Carrier Frequency-Domain Equalization (SC-FDE), can improve spectral efficiency and mitigate interference in overlapping service transmissions across geographically dispersed ground stations.
reference_context: The reference context provides various statistics on the coverage areas with no reliable 2G signal, including 0.3% in England, 1.5% in rural Scotland, and 24.3% in urban Scotland.
